Threat.value: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
I feel like I am only remembering parts of what happened and the rest is missing
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
I can no longer trust my own body
I can't trust that I will do the right thing

issues.explanation: For a 45-year-old male with trauma type toxic chemical exposure, the selected appraisals are mostly danger- and mistrust-focused, but 'I have no future' is more characteristic of pervasive depressive hopelessness or foreshortened future after interpersonal/war trauma. It is not impossible, but here it sits awkwardly with the rest of the profile, which is tightly organized around ongoing threat, body-based reactivity, and fragmented trauma memory. Given the formulation, Threat and Memory strongly drive Negative Appraisals, so the appraisals should plausibly emerge from those nodes; 'Mistrust' and 'Fear of Harm' fit that pattern, whereas 'Hopelessness' is comparatively disconnected from the specific chemical-exposure threat and the other selected items.

For toxic chemical exposure, these two appraisals imply an interpersonal assault/betrayal threat schema ('people can't be trusted', 'who will harm you') rather than a coherent non-interpersonal contamination/exposure trauma formulation. They are hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which centers on bodily danger, somatic reactivity, and fragmented/alien trauma memory.

'Waking Alert: I wake during the night to check whether I am safe' implies a concrete ongoing external-danger monitoring pattern typical of threat from assault, intrusion, or persecution. For toxic chemical exposure, this can be coherent if linked to contamination, breathing, or environmental safety cues, but that link is absent from the rest of the profile.

'Fear of Harm: You can never know who will harm you' is poorly matched to toxic chemical exposure because it frames threat as interpersonal ('who') rather than environmental/toxic exposure. It also does not align well with the other selected items, which are centered on bodily reactions, somatic mistrust, and dissociative/incomplete trauma memory rather than fear of people.

issues.item: Intrusion Monitoring: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
issues.explanation: 'Intrusion Monitoring' implies fear of a human intruder entering the home, which is hard to reconcile with the indexed trauma of toxic chemical exposure and with the rest of the profile, which is centered on bodily danger and trauma-memory phenomena rather than interpersonal threat.

issues.item: Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted
issues.explanation: 'Self-Blame' is weakly supported by the rest of the selected items and is hard to fit with toxic chemical exposure in this profile. The other appraisals focus on the body as damaged/unreliable; blaming one's own actions for a toxic exposure is not impossible, but here it is the main discordant appraisal and lacks support from the threat and memory items.
